post_text:
At 25, Alan Leibman was the youngest general manager in The Ritz-Carlton's history. He is back, as CEO of its yachts.

@The Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection named him chief executive on 10 November. He also joins the board, succeeding Ernesto Fara.

His career began in 1990 at The Ritz-Carlton in Houston. He later ran Kerzner International as CEO, the company behind Atlantis and One&Only, then advised groups across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and the investor Oaktree.

@Tatiana Ferreira, until now Chief Sales Officer, becomes President. She adds IT, marketing and guest experience to sales. Before the sea, she worked for Louis Vuitton, Neiman Marcus and Starwood.

The fleet: three yachts, Evrima, Ilma and Luminara, with itineraries in the Mediterranean and Northern Europe.

Executive Chairman @Jim Murren and @Marriott International CEO @Anthony Capuano both welcomed the appointment. Leibman's own words: "The Ritz-Carlton has been an important part of my career since the beginning."

The signal: at sea too, luxury hands the helm to a hotelier.

Would you swap a week in a resort for a week on a Ritz-Carlton yacht?
